newsitem.title: ITALY: Suntan lotion used to rub in rich-poor gap.
newsitem.headline: Suntan lotion used to rub in rich-poor gap.

text.p: Suntan lotion became a factor at a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit on Wednesday when a Western Samoan rubbed in the differences separating rich and poor.
The Pacific state's deputy prime minister Tuilaepa Sailele Malielegaoi urged countries, especially industrialised nations, to do more to cut emissions that contribute to global warming.
He told the summit that the "Greenhouse Effect" was a threat not only to tender skins but also to food production.

"We constantly see advertisements in the industrialised countries warning against staying out in the sun for more than 15 or so minutes, usually on the beach, unless all exposed parts are liberally covered with sun screen lotion," he said.
"Our poor farmers cannot afford sun screen lotion day in and day out and, if they are going to achieve any production results, they must stay in the sun much, much longer.
"While the illustration is presented lightheartedly I think the danger is real with substantial costs in production losses not to count the medical bill of treating skin cancers."
References to the divide between opulence and suffering in the world have peppered speeches at the summit, taking place at the headquarters of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation.

FAO has faced sharp cuts to its budget and Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe said the agency was owed more than $200 million by member states. "Some of these...clearly have the capacity to pay but lack the political will to do so," he said.
FAO director general Jacques Diouf put it another way.

The budget, he said, "in fact amounts to less than what nine developed countries spend on dog and cat food in six days and, listen to me, less than five percent of what the inhabitants of one developed country spend each year on slimming products to counter the effects of over-eating".
